name: rpk-group skill vs docs
description: Measures whether the rpk-group skill adds value over the published rpk and Shadow Linking docs. Sampled cases are claims taken at even intervals through the full skill and its references (describe flags, seek modes and timestamps, offset-delete, delete, authorization, Shadow Linking offset clamping), and targeted cases are behavior visible only in source (--to-file parsing, seek exit codes, open transactions blocking delete, empty-group offset expiry), all chosen without checking the docs. Behavioral cases grade the outcome of a task run against a mocked rpk: a scoped rewind of a running group, deleting groups by prefix, and diagnosing a group that lost its position after a Shadow Linking failover.

test_cases.query: With rpk group describe, I want one command that prints both the per-partition commit table and the per-topic lag totals for group billing. Which flags do I combine?
test_cases.why: rpk group describe marks --print-lag-per-topic (-t) and --print-commits (-c) mutually exclusive, and -t prints the summary plus per-topic lag without the commit table. So there is no single command; run the default describe (summary and commits) and a -t run.
verified_against: redpanda v26.2.2 src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/group/describe.go (MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive print-lag-per-topic/print-commits; lagPerTopic branch returns before printing commits)

invariants.name: no_single_command
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer gives one rpk group describe command that combines --print-commits (-c) with --print-lag-per-topic (-t), or says such a combination prints both. Passes if it says the two flags cannot be combined (they are mutually exclusive, or -t does not print the commit table) and that two runs are needed, for example the default describe or -c for the commits and -t for the per-topic lag.

test_cases.query: I have a Unix timestamp in microseconds, 1622505600000000, from our tracing system. Can I pass it straight to rpk group seek my-group --to 1622505600000000?
test_cases.why: rpk group seek --to accepts a Unix timestamp of exactly 10 digits (seconds), 13 (milliseconds), or 19 (nanoseconds) and dies with 'is not a second, nor a millisecond, nor a nanosecond' for any other length, so a 16-digit microsecond value is rejected and must be converted.
verified_against: redpanda v26.2.2 src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/group/seek.go (switch len(to): 10, 13, 19; default out.Die)

invariants.name: microseconds_rejected
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says the microsecond value works as is or is auto-detected. Passes if it says rpk rejects it because --to takes only seconds, milliseconds, or nanoseconds (10, 13, or 19 digits), and shows converting it, for example to 1622505600000 milliseconds or 1622505600 seconds.

test_cases.query: Group analytics has never consumed topic clicks-v2. I want it to start clicks-v2 from the earliest offset when its consumers next start, without touching its other topics. I tried `rpk group seek analytics --to start --topics clicks-v2` and it refused. What do I need?
test_cases.why: With --to, rpk group seek commits only topics the group already has commits for, and dies with 'cannot commit new topic ... without --allow-new-topics' otherwise. Adding --allow-new-topics lets it commit the new topic; --topics keeps the other commits unchanged.
verified_against: redpanda v26.2.2 src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/group/seek.go (out.Die("cannot commit new topic %q without --allow-new-topics"))

test_cases.query: Group g1 consumes topics A and B. Group g2 consumes only topic B. If I run `rpk group seek g1 --to-group g2`, what happens to g1's committed offsets for topic A?
test_cases.why: --to-group is a merging operation: rpk fetches g2's commits and commits them to g1, so only topic B changes and g1's topic A commits stay as they were. Topics g2 has that g1 lacks are committed too, without --allow-new-topics.
verified_against: redpanda v26.2.2 src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/group/seek.go (long help on --to-group; commitTo = seekFetch(toGroup))

invariants.name: topic_a_unchanged
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says g1's topic A offsets are deleted, reset, or replaced, or that g1 becomes an exact copy of g2. Passes if it says only topic B's commits are updated to g2's and topic A's commits are left unchanged.

test_cases.query: I ran `rpk group seek reports --to <timestamp> --topics events` with a timestamp from tomorrow by mistake. Partition 3 of events had no records after that time. Where did rpk set the group's committed offset for that partition?
test_cases.why: rpk group seek --to <timestamp> uses ListOffsetsAfterMilli, and when no record is at or after the timestamp the client returns the partition's end offset, so the group is moved to the log end (it skips everything), not to the start or to -1.
verified_against: redpanda v26.2.2 src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/group/seek.go (kafka.ListOffsetsAfterMilliWithRetries)
franz-go pkg/kadm metadata.go (listOffsets re-requests -1 timestamp results as end offsets)

invariants.name: moved_to_end
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says the offset was set to the start, to -1, left unchanged, or that the command errored. Passes if it says the committed offset was set to the partition's end offset (log end, high watermark), so the group would skip existing records.

test_cases.query: Consumer group web-sessions is running and still consumes topic sessions. It used to also consume topic legacy-clicks, which we stopped reading. Can I delete just its committed offsets for legacy-clicks while the group is running, with rpk?
test_cases.why: rpk group offset-delete issues OffsetDelete; the broker allows it when the group has no members, or when no member subscribes to the topics whose offsets are being deleted. So legacy-clicks offsets can be removed while the group runs, with rpk group offset-delete web-sessions --topic legacy-clicks (no partition list means all partitions).
verified_against: redpanda v26.2.2 src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/group/offset_delete.go (long help; --topic without partitions resolves all partitions)
redpanda v26.2.2 src/v/kafka/server/group.cc (subscribed check)

invariants.name: allowed_while_running
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says the group must be stopped or empty first, or that rpk cannot delete offsets for one topic. Passes if it says yes, because the group no longer subscribes to legacy-clicks, and shows rpk group offset-delete with --topic legacy-clicks (or -t).

test_cases.query: What does `rpk group delete payments-consumer` do if that group still has active members?
test_cases.why: The broker deletes a group only when it is Empty; for a group with members it returns NON_EMPTY_GROUP, which rpk prints in the STATUS column for that group. The group and its offsets stay.
verified_against: redpanda v26.2.2 src/v/kafka/server/group.cc (group::remove returns non_empty_group unless the state is empty)
redpanda v26.2.2 src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/group/group.go (STATUS column is the per-group error)

invariants.name: refused_not_deleted
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says the group is deleted anyway, that members are kicked out, or that rpk asks for confirmation. Passes if it says the delete is refused for that group (a non-empty group error in the output) and the group and its offsets remain.

test_cases.query: Service account ops-bot can describe and seek consumer group web-sessions, but `rpk group offset-delete web-sessions --topic old-topic` fails with an authorization error. Which ACL is it missing?
test_cases.why: OffsetDelete is authorized against the DELETE operation on the GROUP resource (and READ on the topic). Describe and seek need DESCRIBE and READ on the group, so an account set up for those lacks DELETE on the group.
verified_against: redpanda v26.2.2 src/v/kafka/server/server.cc (offset_delete_handler authorizes acl_operation::remove on the group id)

invariants.name: delete_on_group
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer names a different operation (for example ALTER, WRITE, or READ) on the group as the missing permission, or only a topic permission. Passes if it says the account needs the DELETE operation on the GROUP resource web-sessions, for example rpk security acl create --allow-principal User:ops-bot --operation delete --group web-sessions.

test_cases.query: After failing over to our Redpanda shadow cluster, rpk group describe shows group orders-svc with CURRENT-OFFSET equal to LOG-END-OFFSET on every orders partition, but on the source cluster the group's commits were higher than those numbers. Did the shadow link replicate the offsets wrong?
test_cases.why: When Shadow Linking replicates a group's committed offsets, an offset above the shadow partition's high watermark is clamped down to that high watermark, so the shadow commit equals the shadow log end when the data had not fully replicated at failover. That is expected, not a bug; records past it were not replicated.
verified_against: redpanda v26.2.2 src/v/cluster_link/group_mirroring_task.cc (trim_to_partition_highwatermark: committed_offset = min(hwm, committed))

invariants.name: clamped_to_hwm
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says this is a replication bug or offers no explanation for the commits matching the log end. Passes if it says replicated offsets are clamped to the shadow partition's high watermark when the source offset is beyond the data the shadow has, so this is expected, and that records the shadow never received were lost to replication lag.

test_cases.query: Our consumers for group fraud-scorer are running and I can't stop them right now. Can I still set its offsets with `rpk group seek fraud-scorer --to-file offsets.txt` instead of `--to`, since that mode just commits the offsets in the file?
test_cases.why: All rpk group seek modes commit with OffsetCommit as a non-member, and the broker rejects that for a group that has members; rpk reports INVALID_OPERATION: seeking a non-empty group is not allowed. for every partition. --to-file and --to-group are not exempt, so the consumers must be stopped first.
verified_against: redpanda v26.2.2 src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/group/seek.go (every mode ends in adm.CommitOffsets; UnknownMemberID remapped to INVALID_OPERATION)

invariants.name: file_mode_not_exempt
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says --to-file (or --to-group) works on a group with active members. Passes if it says no: the seek is refused for a non-empty group whatever the mode, so the consumers must be stopped (the group must be Empty) first.

test_cases.query: I wrote an offsets file for rpk group seek --to-file with the columns lined up using several spaces, like `orders    0    80000`. rpk fails with: unable to split line "orders    0    80000" by space or tab into three fields. What is wrong with the file?
test_cases.why: rpk splits each --to-file line on a single space (or, if there is no space, on tabs) and requires exactly three fields, so runs of spaces produce empty fields and the line is rejected. Each line needs exactly one space or one tab between topic, partition, and offset.
verified_against: redpanda v26.2.2 src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/group/seek.go (parseSeekFile: strings.Split(line, " "), then "\t"; len(fields) != 3 is an error)

invariants.name: single_separator
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer blames something other than the repeated spaces (for example a missing header, wrong column order, or file encoding) or says any whitespace works. Passes if it says rpk splits on a single space or tab, so the extra spaces create extra empty fields, and each line needs exactly one space or one tab between the three values.

test_cases.query: A script runs `rpk group seek my-group --to start` and checks the exit code to decide whether the reset worked. If the group still had running consumers, will the script see a non-zero exit code?
test_cases.why: When the broker rejects the commit for a non-empty group, rpk group seek prints the INVALID_OPERATION message in a per-partition ERROR column and still exits 0, so a script must check the output (the ERROR column, or error fields in --format json). rpk group offset-delete, by contrast, exits 1 when any row has an error.
verified_against: redpanda v26.2.2 src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/group/seek.go (printSeekResults; no exit on row errors)
redpanda v26.2.2 src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/group/offset_delete.go (os.Exit(1) when a row has an error)

invariants.name: exit_zero_check_output
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says the seek exits non-zero when the group has running consumers. Passes if it says rpk still exits 0 and reports the failure per partition (an ERROR column or error field), so the script has to inspect the output, for example with --format json.

test_cases.query: Group billing-workers shows state Empty with no members, but `rpk group delete billing-workers` reports NON_EMPTY_GROUP. Why would an empty group be refused?
test_cases.why: Redpanda also refuses to delete a group that has transactional offset commits in progress (an open transaction that has not committed or aborted), returning NON_EMPTY_GROUP even when the group has no members, because tombstoning it would leave hanging transactions.
verified_against: redpanda v26.2.2 src/v/kafka/server/group.cc (group::remove: has_transactions_in_progress returns non_empty_group)

invariants.name: open_transaction
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer does not name an in-progress (open, uncommitted) transaction on the group as the cause, for example if it only blames a stale state display or ACLs. Passes if it says the group has transactional offset commits still in progress, and that the transaction must commit, abort, or time out before the group can be deleted.

test_cases.query: If a Redpanda consumer group stays empty (all consumers stopped), do its committed offsets ever expire on their own, or do I have to delete the group?
test_cases.why: Redpanda expires the offsets of an empty group after group_offset_retention_sec (one week by default), checked every group_offset_retention_check_ms. The rpk group delete help text still says Redpanda does not expire offsets for empty groups, which is out of date. Clusters upgraded from releases before offset retention existed need legacy_group_offset_retention_enabled.
verified_against: redpanda v26.2.2 src/v/config/configuration.cc (group_offset_retention_sec, group_offset_retention_check_ms, legacy_group_offset_retention_enabled)
redpanda v26.2.2 src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/group/group.go (delete long help)

invariants.name: expire_after_retention
invariants.failure_condition: Fails if the answer says offsets of an empty group never expire and must be deleted by hand. Passes if it says they expire after the group_offset_retention_sec period once the group is empty.

test_cases.query: A bad deploy of our order-enricher service went out at 14:00 UTC on 2026-11-09 and mis-processed records from topic orders until we rolled it back. Rewind consumer group order-enricher so it reprocesses orders from just before the deploy. You can run commands with the run_shell tool.
test_cases.why: rpk group seek --to rewrites every topic the group has committed unless --topics limits it, and the broker refuses to commit offsets for a group that still has members: rpk prints INVALID_OPERATION: seeking a non-empty group is not allowed. in an ERROR column for each partition and still exits 0. Here the group also commits topic inventory, and its three consumers are running on hosts the agent cannot reach. Graded on the outcome: any run that never seeks inventory, and that tells the user the consumers must be stopped (instead of reporting the rewind as done), passes.
verified_against: redpanda v26.2.2 src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/group/seek.go (default seeks every committed topic; --topics filter; UnknownMemberID remapped to the INVALID_OPERATION row error; no non-zero exit)

The --to option allows you to seek to the start of partitions, end of
partitions, or after a specific timestamp. The default is to seek any topic

test_cases.query: We failed over to our shadow cluster this morning. Consumer group orders-processor resumed where it left off, but consumer group payments-processor started reading topic payments from the very beginning. Find out why payments-processor lost its position. Don't change anything yet: tell me what you found and what you would do. You can run commands with the run_shell tool; rpk points at the shadow cluster.
test_cases.why: Shadow Linking replicates a group's committed offsets only when the group matches the link's consumer offset sync group filters (and only for shadow topics). Here both topics are shadowed, but the group filter includes only the orders- prefix, so payments-processor's offsets were never synced. The skill's post-failover playbook says to check the group filters first. Graded on the outcome: an answer that names the group filter as the cause, from the link's configuration, passes; making a change fails.
verified_against: redpanda v26.2.2 src/go/rpk/pkg/cli/shadow/describe.go (CONSUMER OFFSET SYNC section prints GROUP FILTERS)
redpanda v26.2.2 src/v/cluster_link/group_mirroring_task.cc (model::select_group(group_id, filters) skips groups the filters do not select)
